Suicide Prevention & Mental Wellness Workshops
Suicide claims the lives of too many people in agriculture. The Minnesota Farm Suicide Prevention Campaign invites you to attend free workshops that teach anyone who lives or works in an agricultural community how to help when they see someone struggling.
Please consider investing 2 hours of your time in learning more about mental wellness and suicide prevention.
Workshops are scheduled for Ada, Albert Lea, Austin, Buffalo, Cloquet, Crookston, Fergus Falls, Grand Rapids, Marshall, Mora, New Ulm, Rochester, Thief River Falls, Waite Park, Willmar, and Worthington Minnesota from mid- September through late October. Go to QPR/COMET workshops for dates, locations, and registration
Who should attend?
Farmers, farm family members, crop consultants, ag. lenders, insurance adjusters, Extension educators, county or township officials, rural clergy, state or federal agency staff, veterinarians, ag coop staff and board members, grain elevator staff, and anyone else who lives or works in a rural area.
What will I learn?
(Note: you can attend either or both workshops)
1: QPR (Question, Persuade, Refer) for Agriculture is a 2-hour evidence-based workshop that teaches three steps to help you recognize warning signs, engage in supportive conversations, and connect someone at risk to appropriate care and life-saving resources. This workshop can serve as an introduction to suicide prevention or as a “refresher” for people who have taken a suicide prevention training in the past.
2: COMET (Changing Our Mental and Emotional Trajectory) is a 2-hour interactive workshop that will teach you how to start a caring conversation with someone who seems sad, withdrawn, or not quite themselves. You’ll learn 7 questions that can help someone who may be moving toward a mental health crisis turn their trajectory back toward a place of wellness.
How do I find a workshop near me and sign up?
Go to QPR/COMET Workshops .
Questions? Contact Meg at 651-201-6616 or meg.moynihan@state.mn.us

Website Domain Change Coming Soon
Freeborn County will soon be transitioning its website domain from .com to .gov .
This change is being made to enhance security, improve public trust, and clearly identify the website as an official government resource. During the transition, the current website address will continue to function and visitors will be automatically redirected to the new .gov website.
No action is required by residents at this time.
Thank you for your patience as we work to improve access to County information and services.
County Board Meetings
County Board meetings will no longer be livestreamed. However, meetings will continue to be recorded and made available on the County website shortly after adjournment. Closed captioning will be included on all posted recordings under "Commissioner Videos" located below in Popular Resources.
